title: "set_dvs_threads()"
subtitle: "Set the process-wide thread pool size"
format:
  html:
    keep-md: true

  freeze: auto
---

`set_dvs_threads()` sets how many threads dvs uses for parallel file operations
(`dvs_add()`, `dvs_get()`, `dvs_status()`). The value is stored as the
`dvs.num_threads` option and synced to the dvs core before each operation. It is
process-wide. There is no per-call thread argument in R.

```r
set_dvs_threads(threads)
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `threads` | integer(1) or `NULL` | required | A whole number of threads from 1 to 32, or `NULL` or `0` to set no thread count. `NA`, a negative or fractional number, a number above 32, `TRUE`, `FALSE`, a string or more than one value raises a `dvs_error_argument`. |

Returns the previous value invisibly.

## Which thread count an operation uses

Each `dvs_add()`, `dvs_get()` and `dvs_status()` takes its thread count from
the first rule that applies:

1. A thread count set with `set_dvs_threads()` or in the `dvs.num_threads`
   option: that many threads.
2. The `DVS_NUM_THREADS` environment variable, when it is a whole number above
   0: that many threads, at most 32. A larger value uses 32. Any other value is
   ignored.
3. Otherwise 4 threads per CPU, at most 16.

An operation never uses more threads than it has files.

## Setup

```{r}
options(width = 1000)
library(dvs)
```

## Set a fixed thread count

Set a fixed number of threads. It takes effect on the next add, get, or status.

```{r}
set_dvs_threads(2)
getOption("dvs.num_threads")
```

## More than 32

A count above 32 is refused, and the option keeps its value:

```{r}
#| error: true
set_dvs_threads(33)
getOption("dvs.num_threads")
```

A `dvs.num_threads` above 32 set with `options()` is refused the same way, by
the next `dvs_add()`, `dvs_get()` or `dvs_status()`:
`` `options(dvs.num_threads)` must be at most 32 ``.

## Reset to automatic

Pass `NULL` or `0` to set no thread count. The next operation then takes
`DVS_NUM_THREADS`, or else 4 threads per CPU, at most 16.

```{r}
set_dvs_threads(NULL)
getOption("dvs.num_threads")
```

## Differences from the CLI

The CLI sets threads per call with `--threads <N>`, and the R setting is
process-wide. `--threads` takes the same values: 1 to 32, or `0` for no count.
A count above 32 or below 0 exits with code 2, for example
`33 is not in 0..=32`, and is `invalid_arguments` under `--json`. Threads set
directly on either surface win. The
`DVS_NUM_THREADS` environment variable applies only when neither the CLI flag
nor `set_dvs_threads()` has set a count. See the `--threads` flag on any
[CLI command](cli-init.html).
